# Pi-Bench

Long-horizon personal-assistant work for five role personas: research, marketing, pharmacy, legal training and finance, with hidden intents and a persistent workspace.

## Good to know

- A unit is one persona; its 20 tasks run in the upstream's episode order, share a workspace and use earlier tasks' artifacts. Run all five personas for the 100-task benchmark.
- The user is the upstream's hidden-intent simulator: it probes for requirements the opening request does not state, so several turns per task are normal.
- The reward is COMP, the upstream checklist score; PROC, the hidden-intent coverage score, is reported beside it in the job.
- The persona's AppWorld tools come from the official image, one container per unit. The image's own nanobot harness is not used.
- Pull zzzhr97/pi-bench:latest before a run: it supplies AppWorld for the tools. A machine without Docker can answer text-only turns but cannot use the persona's apps.
- Pi-Bench declares a simulated user and a judge, so a provider key is needed before any run, including the nop control.
- Scoring runs an LLM judge over every task's trace; give the score phase time with --timeout score=3600 when a full persona is evaluated.

## Upstream limitations

- The official harness ships its own nanobot agent and a Docker image; it exposes no interface for an arbitrary agent. This entry substitutes the Nullius agent under test and uses the image only for AppWorld.
- Twenty-four tasks declare AppWorld tool use; the rest still run in an AppWorld-backed persona and may use the persona's apps.
- The benchmark has no published reference solution, so no oracle control is declared.

## Nullius limitations

- A unit is a whole persona, not one task: a run reports five units for 100 tasks, and a single persona is a dataset of its own.
- The agent under test must prove AppWorld tools, conversation and a workspace; an agent without the tools port cannot run the tool tasks.
- The official image's harness entrypoint is not used; the driver starts only its AppWorld API and serves the upstream's MCP server, so image-level harness changes are not picked up.
- The official evaluator's own trace and log conventions are reproduced by the driver from the Nullius transcript; tool calls themselves are not rendered, as the upstream trace configuration does not render them.
